scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Legend holds that the Saraya dance originated after the victory of gods and goddesses over giants and demons, symbolizing war weapons.
Rituals begin on Saptami when an alam (image of God) decorated with colored flags is brought to the temple or kot after flowers are collected.
The dance may have originally served to protect valuable statues and weapons before evolving into an entertaining Dashain tradition.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Held annually from Ekadashi to Purnima, typically beginning the day after Dashain tika.
The largest performance occurs on the full moon day at Arje Phulbari in Gulmi.
It symbolizes the ancient war and victory of deities over demons.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Practiced across western hilly districts including Gulmi, Arghakhanchi, Pyuthan, Palpa, Kapilvastu, Rupandehi, and Dang, with prominent local participation in Dhurkot, Arje, and Isma.
Classified as a folk dance of Nepal, maintaining deep ties to temple rituals and Dashain festival traditions.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The dance is tied to sacred temple rituals starting on Saptami involving an alam (image of God) and offerings to deities; outsiders must respect local religious shrines and temple protocols.
